ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute with no refund: the surge notice was complete and timely, so the $21.14 metered fare stands. No account flag, no driver reminder (no route deviation arises — billed distance equals the optimal route).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was billed at $21.14 against a $16.26 upfront quote, the $4.88 gap coming from a surge multiplier rise from 1× to 1.4× between quote and trip start, which the surge log records [F6][F7][F8]. A rise in surge with a rider who then rode is governed by SURGE-2, and the outcome turns on whether the notice required by SURGE-1 was given [F9][SURGE-2].

The notice in the log was sent in-app at 17:14:45, before the 17:16:00 trip start, and reads: "Fares are 1.4× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $22.48. Free cancellation until 17:13." [F9]. It states the new multiplier (1.4×), a revised estimated fare ($22.48), and free cancellation — the three items SURGE-1 requires [F9][SURGE-1]. SURGE-1 asks only that the notice STATE a revised estimated fare, and an estimate that differs from the fare finally charged (here $22.48 quoted versus $21.14 metered) is still a stated estimate; the $4.88 the fare exceeds the quote by is therefore not a non-notification case.

Two things do not disturb that reading. The rider's own messages in the chat concern only the taxi stand and the car, and say nothing about surge or fare [F10][F11][F12]. The driver's after-trip statement that the rider was told and chose to ride [F13] is corroborative only and is not needed, since the platform log settles notice on its own. No route deviation is in issue either: billed distance 5.6 km does not exceed the 5.6 km optimal route, so deviation is 0.0 km and RD-1's tolerance bars any route refund [F1][F3][RD-1].

Safety screen: I read all chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint. Nothing describes threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks, dangerous driving, an accident or anyone feeling unsafe — the messages are ordinary pickup arrangements [F10][F11][F13].

Because the notice was complete, the higher fare stands under SURGE-2 and there is no refundable sum: the surge differential the rider seeks ((1.4 − 1) × $14.05 = $5.62, capped at the $4.88 the fare exceeds the quote by) is not refundable when notice was given [F8][SURGE-3]. The record settles every element: the platform's notification log is timestamped, the fare build-up is itemised, and no record is missing.
